stage: densified driving — the same dance, 81 samples over the identical duration
registered_by: executor seat, on E10-density, before the first submission of any E10 graph
how_these_were_chosen: The date as a plain integer with a run index appended, continuing the rule specs/E09-seeds.json, specs/E09-A3-seeds.json and specs/E08-seeds.json use: 2026-08-12, runs 21 and 22. The property that matters is that both numbers are fixed BEFORE any result is seen, and a date-derived seed is checkable against this file's own git timestamp. Neither seed was drawn from a prior run, from any served template, or from anything this seat had already looked at.

allocation.2026081221: the probe — the one generation this spec authorises up front
allocation.2026081222: reserve, spendable only on a named cause the probe surfaces

why_the_index_starts_at_21: specs/E09-A3-seeds.json registered 2026081201-02 and specs/E08-seeds.json registered 2026081211-13 on this same calendar day. Reusing any of those numbers would put a seed registered for one experiment onto another, and the record would afterwards have to explain which run a number belonged to. The offset keeps every seed on this rig traceable to exactly one registration.
why_a_new_seed_at_all_when_everything_el: A new frame count is a new generation. The Animate route's latent is sized 832x480x81 here against 832x480x65 in E08, so the sampler's noise tensor has a different shape and the same integer would not reproduce E08's noise field even in principle. Registering a fresh number states that plainly rather than implying a same-seed comparison the route cannot deliver.

ceiling.note: 2 generations — 1 probe plus 1 reserve on a named cause. estimate_credits is re-confirmed before the first submission and both meters are reported; on an all-OSS graph it returns 0 by construction (E08 §12), so the ceiling is enforced by counting generations. Spent credits have no compensator; the bound is the honest treatment.
ceiling.why_machine_readable: The value was free prose and no tool under tools/ read the key, while `seeds` and `allocation` — its machine-readable siblings — are both consumed and gated. CLAUDE.md makes the credit ceiling a per-spec obligation and records that spent credits have no compensator, so the one unrecoverable resource in this repo was bounded by a string nothing could parse. The prose is not deleted: it is `note`, verbatim, and the number a submission step can count against sits beside it. CORRECTION, 2026-09-04 (swarm wave 8, F-6c5c537b). This paragraph used to argue the fix with the clause “while `seeds` and `allocation` — its machine-readable siblings — are both consumed and gated”, and to close “and the number a submission step can count against sits beside it”. Both halves were measured on the tree and only one survived. `grep -rn allocation tools/ --include=*.py` returns 0 hits: `allocation` has no reader at all, so it is exactly as unread as `ceiling` was when it was filed. `seeds` has seven readers — build_animate_payload.py:482 (main), build_camera_i2v_payload.py:1110 (main), build_i2v_payload.py:620 (main), build_lora_arm_payload.py:463 (gate_s), build_r2v_payload.py:217 (build_and_write), build_t2v_payload.py:496 (main) and gate_saved_graph.py:487 (main) — each handing the list to a seed gate, so that half of the claim holds. And no tool reads `ceiling` from a seeds spec either: every `ceiling` hit under tools/ is `armature_core.assembly`'s unrelated CASCADE slot ceiling, or a builder passing that one. So `ceiling.submissions` is a number a submission step COULD count against and none does today — the bound is held by the spec and the executor, not by code. The original claim is kept above rather than deleted, because the correction is more useful than the original. tests/test_seeds_specs.py pins the measurement; the day a builder counts against `ceiling.submissions`, that test flips with it and this paragraph is rewritten again.

binds_in_both_directions: An experiment that pre-registered seeds must use one of them, and an experiment that pre-registered none may not vary its seed at all. tools/armature_core/gates.py::gate_s_seed_registration enforces both clauses at build time and tools/armature_core/route_gates.py::gate_s_registration enforces them again against the graph that is about to run.
